title: Determining wavelength with a diffraction grating

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and planned figures are original. P2 evidence supplies grating calculation, symmetry, comparison and multi-step demand patterns only. No P1 lesson assignment inferred.

questions.prompt: State the diffraction-grating equation taught in Lesson 10 and state what the order number n represents.
A student measures 58.2° between matching second-order maxima. What value of θ should be used in d sin θ = nλ?
Why is the separation between matching left and right maxima measured instead of relying on one angle from the centre?

options.B: Its midpoint reduces dependence on a small zero-direction offset.

questions.prompt: Which procedure gives the strongest evidence about random variation in the angular measurement?

options.B: Copy the same displayed reading three times.
options.C: Re-find both matching maxima independently and repeat their separation.
options.D: Use an unidentified maximum at the largest visible angle.

questions.prompt: Describe how to determine the wavelength of single-frequency light using a diffraction grating of known spacing. Your method must use angular measurements on both sides of the central maximum and repeated readings.
A grating has 450 lines per millimetre. Three measurements of the separation between the left and right third-order maxima are 50.6°, 50.9° and 50.7°.
